| [CASE-121](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-121.md) | One melody from a 1951 gospel record to a 2005 Katrina protest song: "I've Got a Savior", "I Got a Woman", "Gold Digger" and "George Bush Doesn't Care About Black People", each link a different relation, the message turned at every step | Boyle's chain in The Public Domain, ch. 6 ([LIT-1301](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1301.md)). The Bailey Gospel Singers' "I've Got a Savior" (c. 1951), reworded by Ray Charles as "I Got a Woman" (1955), re-sung by Jamie Foxx as the licensed hook of Kanye West's "Gold Digger" (2005), looped from that recording by The Legendary K.O. for a Katrina protest song. The melody and phrase pattern carry through; the object of praise turns from a saviour to a generous woman, a mercenary one, then a president's indifference. Each link is a different relation: rewording, licensed re-performance, sampling. The received origin story was wrong, and the melody found the real source. | Active |
